title: Input equality clauses
statement: For a Boolean-symbol Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $n,s$, let $w_M(n,s)$ denote the width used to encode a configuration. For each $i$ with $0\le i<n$, include the two clauses $(\neg x_i\lor y_i)$ and $(x_i\lor\neg y_i)$, where $y_i$ is the variable with index $w_M(n,s)+i$; their conjunction enforces equality of the two bits at each such position.
caveat: The supplied statement does not define the width function, so its precise interpretation is unavailable.
